request.system:
You are the Outcomes agent. A company earlier announced job cuts (summary below). You read one of
its LATER filings and record what the company itself reports about the results of that restructuring.
Record claims only, copied VERBATIM. Never infer results, never use boilerplate (forward-looking statements,
risk factors, safe-harbor text) and never use statements about unrelated programs.

Kinds:
- savings_achieved: savings or efficiencies the company says it has realized
- savings_expected: savings or benefits it still expects
- charges: restructuring or severance costs it reports for this program
- problem: difficulties it reports (delays, higher costs, disruption, attrition, customer impact)
- reversal: re-hiring, reversing or scaling back the cuts
- other: any other reported result of the program

Return ONE JSON object:
{
  "relates_to_program": true | false,   // does this filing report on the same restructuring?
  "outcomes": [ {"kind": "...", "quote": "verbatim sentence", "amount_text": "verbatim amount or null"} ],
  "notes": "one short sentence"
}
At most 5 outcomes. Output JSON only.

oRestructuring program implemented with positive P&L and cash flow impacts expected in the second half of the year and beyond

•Cash position was €121.5 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with €109.7 million as of December 31, 2025. This strong cash position reflects the positive impact of restructuring initiatives, disciplined cash management and €37 million in gross proceeds from the successful reserved offering completed in the second quarter of 2026.

•Valneva successfully implemented a global restructuring initiative4 to reduce its cash burn through a significant workforce reduction, the reprioritization and rescheduling of R&D activities and the streamlining of its global operations. As part of this initiative, the Company also agreed to sell its Nantes site in France for €6.2 million. A preliminary sale agreement has been signed with Nantes Métropole, and the transaction is expected to close in September 2026.

Peter Bühler, Valneva’s Chief Financial Officer, commented, “Our focus over the past few months, following the Lyme VALOR results has been to restructure and refocus our operations. The successful financing completed in April has enabled us to build and maintain a strong cash position, allowing us to prioritize resources on our core business and key strategic priorities while preserving the flexibility to accelerate growth should the Lyme program progress successfully toward licensure and commercialization.”

In the first half of 2026, €3.2 million of expenses were recognized across the affected functions in connection with the workforce reduction and restructuring program initiated in the second quarter of 2026.
